Students also passed a package of 40 constitutional amendments 1,193 to 262 and voted 1,019 to 669 to ask the Board of Regents to institute a $9 per semester Talisman yearbook fee. Mason Stevenson and Melissa Paris won the two vice presidencies unopposed, and all 25 senate candidates on the ballot were elected.

events.title: SGA funded the Buy-A-Book program
events.body: SGA passed legislation 22-2 on April 5 allocating $2,000 to the Buy-A-Book program, and the University Bookstore pledged to match the amount. The bill by senator Katharine Pettit was amended unanimously to help 20 students who needed financial assistance buying textbooks instead of 10. Recipients were to be chosen by the academic affairs committee based on a required essay and need.

events.title: Goodrum found not guilty in Katie Autry murder trial
events.body: A jury in Owensboro found Lucas Goodrum, 23, of Scottsville not guilty of the May 2003 murder of Pellville freshman Melissa "Katie" Autry, who was set on fire in her Poland Hall dorm room and died three days later. The verdict came March 21 after three hours of deliberation, ending a three-week trial that had been moved from Warren County. Stephen Soules had earlier pleaded guilty to murder, rape, sodomy, arson and robbery and expected life in prison.

leaders.name: Katie Dawson
leaders.note: Named in April 2004 Herald coverage as incoming executive vice president, so she came up through the cabinet.
profile: Dawson served as both SGA president and student regent during Western's centennial year. When the university launched its 14-month centennial celebration on Nov. 19, 2005, she spoke at the dedication of Centennial Plaza, offering her own meaning for the school slogan: "Find what you love and carry it with you your whole life through."

Her spring semester was dominated by a proposed $46-per-semester fee for three campus construction projects. At a student forum with President Gary Ransdell she suggested exempting the next year's seniors, who would graduate before any project was finished; the Board of Regents rejected the exemption 10-1 at its April 7 meeting and approved the fee 9-1. Dawson cast the lone abstention, saying that although she supported the fee, she could not vote for it with so many seniors counting on the exemption.

Her term ended at Western's 159th commencement on May 13, 2006, where the Radcliff native graduated with a degree in corporate and organizational communication and addressed her 1,797 fellow undergraduates as SGA president. She charged the graduates to have courage, endurance, strength, patience and character, saying success was knowing "when to throw in the towel and when to wave it around and cheer."

events.title: The plus/minus grading fight
events.body: An Institutional Research report on plus and minus grading, a protest broadside, a post-winter-term student survey and an SGA handbook all survive - one of the few academic-policy campaigns documented from research through to public agitation.

events.title: WKU launched its centennial celebration
events.body: Western kicked off a 14-month celebration of its 1906 founding on Saturday, Nov. 19, dedicating three new campus landmarks including Centennial Plaza. SGA President Katie Dawson spoke at the plaza dedication, offering her own meaning of the school slogan "The Spirit Makes the Master."

events.title: SGA closed the fall with 10 pieces of legislation
events.body: The Herald reported that SGA passed 10 pieces of legislation in the fall semester, fewer than in previous fall semesters. Its legislation brought bikes, a cancer documentary and iPods to Western. The same issue reported that a senator named Johnson had been elected the new speaker of the senate.

events.title: SGA took up a proposed $45 construction fee
events.body: At its first regular meeting of the spring semester, SGA discussed a proposed $45-per-semester fee to pay for a campus-wide wireless network, a new health center and renovations to the Ivan Wilson Center for Fine Arts. President Katie Dawson supported the fee, and Western's chief financial officer estimated it would raise about $1.4 million a year.

events.title: Ransdell asked SGA for a resolution backing the fee
events.body: WKU President Gary Ransdell came to the SGA meeting and urged senators to pass a resolution supporting the proposed $45 fee, which the Board of Regents would vote on April 7. Dawson sat on that board as student regent, and SGA officers said a supporting resolution was likely within a few weeks.

events.title: Executive vice president aired an internal rift
events.body: Executive Vice President Mason Stevenson read a letter at the SGA meeting saying some members trying to protect their political interests had "thwarted" SGA's mission to improve Western. The letter outlined his concerns about relations between the executive and legislative branches.

events.title: Senate put $2,000 toward SGA's 40th anniversary party
events.body: Two bills devoting $2,000 to a party for SGA's 40th anniversary passed unanimously at the group's Tuesday meeting. The Herald reported the organization planned a campus-wide party to mark four decades of student government at Western.

events.title: Regents approved the fee; Dawson's senior exemption failed
events.body: The Board of Regents voted 9-1 to approve the $46-per-semester construction fee, with Dawson abstaining, and rejected 10-1 her proposal to exempt next year's seniors, an idea she had raised at a student forum the week before. Dawson said that although she supported the fee, she could not vote for it with so many seniors counting on the exemption.

events.title: Rob Watkins elected SGA president
events.body: Bowling Green senior Robert Watkins won the online election for SGA president after spending more than a week seeking supporters who would vote on TopNet. He defeated Berea junior Kara Ratliff, and the results were announced Tuesday at a crowded Revolution 91.

events.title: Executive board issued its first veto of the year
events.body: After the Tuesday senate meeting, the SGA executive board vetoed a bill that would have financed community- and campus-oriented projects through civic engagement grants, the first time it exercised its veto power that year. The Herald reported the grants were "a reality for only about 30 minutes" and that time restraints halted an appeal of the veto.

events.title: Herald editorial attacked SGA misspending
events.body: A Herald editorial titled "SGA misspending" said members should not have to be "motivated by a giveaway to show up for meetings." It noted that the opinion page had devoted considerable space in recent weeks to both positive and negative aspects of SGA, which it said could and should be an important organization on campus.

leaders.name: Robert Watkins
leaders.note: Single-year plate and the only name attached to 2006 because Watkins resigned partway through the 2006-07 term; no plate covers the full year. Confirmed against Herald election coverage: a Bowling Green senior, he won the SGA presidency in the 13 April 2006 online election, defeating Berea junior Kara Ratliff. He had been elected the first speaker of the senate under the new constitution on 15 April 2004, a result contested 9-8 and then upheld. He resigned as president and student regent on 28 November 2006, per SGA's own senate minutes for that day's regularly scheduled Tuesday meeting, which record the resignation being read into the record; this site previously followed a Herald account giving the date as 30 November, which this run corrects against the primary minutes.

College Heights Herald 79:53, 20 Apr 2004 - "Robert Watkins Upheld as Speaker"

profile: Robert "Rob" Watkins, a Bowling Green student, wrote the SGA constitution adopted in 2004 and was elected the first speaker of the senate under it on 15 April 2004, defeating Brittany Fausey 9 votes to 8 in a result immediately contested over what quorum the new constitution required; the vote was upheld later that month.

Watkins won the SGA presidency in the 13 April 2006 online election, defeating Berea junior Kara Ratliff after more than a week courting TopNet voters, with results announced at a crowded Revolution 91.7. He took office for 2006-07 alongside Administrative Vice President Amanda Allen, who by October was tightening the budget after the prior administration left roughly $24,000 unspent.

Watkins resigned as SGA president and student regent on 28 November 2006, with the resignation read into the senate's own minutes at that day's regularly scheduled Tuesday meeting, after senators had aired concerns about him at an unannounced 10 p.m. meeting the evening before. (A Herald account this site had followed gave the date as 30 November; the primary senate minutes are treated as authoritative here.) A Herald editorial the same week was headlined "SGA actions an embarrassment to Western." The resignation left students without a voting voice on the Board of Regents for at least a month and put junior Jeanne Johnson in as a fill-in leader for the rest of the term, sworn in at the 5 December Winter Banquet.

events.title: SGA tightened its budget after leaving $24,000 unspent
events.body: The Herald reported that SGA had left about $24,000 of its $115,000 budget unspent at the end of 2005-06, money that returned to Western's general fund. Administrative Vice President Amanda Allen said SGA was cutting money from areas where it went unspent, adding almost $10,000 to organizational aid and $3,000 to the miscellaneous fund. Allen called the previous year a bad budgetary year but also a learning year.

events.title: Watkins resigned as SGA president and student regent
events.body: SGA's own senate minutes record that president and student regent Rob Watkins's resignation was formally read into the meeting at the senate's regularly scheduled Tuesday session, with senators told Jeanne Johnson would be sworn in as president at the Dec. 5 Winter Banquet. Senators had voiced concerns about Watkins at an unannounced 10 p.m. meeting the evening before. A Herald front-page account (Wayback, 2 Dec 2006) covered the same resignation but gave the date as 30 November; this entry follows the primary senate minutes, which date the reading of the resignation to 28 November, leaving students without representation on Western's governing board for at least a month.

events.title: Fill-in SGA leader Jeanne Johnson challenged tuition plan at regents meeting
events.body: The Board of Regents approved a 7.8 percent tuition increase for 2007-08, bringing tuition and fees to $6,417 a year including the higher athletics fee. Jeanne Johnson, a junior economics and finance major from Marion described as a fill-in for the former SGA president, opposed the size of the increase for online and distance-learning courses, though she had no vote. She said 'We know tuition increases are inevitable' but argued distance learners should not carry that burden.

events.title: Provost rejected plus/minus grading; Johnson credited SGA's campaign
events.body: Provost Barbara Burch told the University Senate she would not implement the plus/minus grading system the senate had passed 36-23 in March. SGA President Jeanne Johnson said she was grateful for the decision, noting SGA had raised awareness and led student protests, and pledged that students would keep fighting if the issue returned. She said 'I'm confident that the students' opinions have been expressed.'

events.title: SGA banquet closed the year and swore in 2007-08 officers
events.body: At its annual banquet on May 1, SGA presented awards and swore in officers for 2007-08, with Jeanne Lynn Johnson of Marion becoming the new SGA president and student regent and receiving the Dero Downing Award. Johnathon Boles of Elizabethtown became executive vice president, Kayla Shelton speaker of the Student Senate, and Cherieth Lea Lineweaver administrative vice president. Amanda Beth Allen received the Charles A. Keown Award, SGA's highest honor.

events.title: SGA-run referendum showed students favored the I-A football move
events.body: In an online referendum SGA arranged alongside the homecoming queen election, 64.6 percent of voting students, 1,095, supported WKU's proposed move to Division I-A football, with 600 against. A total of 2,136 students voted in the poll, and the 1,695 who answered the football question represented about 9 percent of enrollment. SGA President Rob Watkins, who held the student seat on the Board of Regents, said the poll would help him define a position but noted the homecoming tie-in likely drew football-friendly voters.

events.title: SGA senate unanimously passed a resolution backing the I-A move
events.body: SGA members unanimously passed a resolution saying they supported the move to Division I-A football, following the student referendum result. Watkins, as student regent and SGA president, still would not say what his own position was before the regents' vote.

events.title: Johnson won the student regent election; SGA seated a full senate
events.body: Jeanne Johnson, SGA president and Marion junior, won the special election for Western's vacant student regent seat with 688 votes, 41 percent of ballots cast. The same Herald issue reported that SGA began the spring semester with its first full senate attendance since fall 2004.

events.title: Senate passed Books for Africa bill and a printing-quota resolution
events.body: At the same Nov. 28 meeting where Watkins's resignation was read into the record, the senate unanimously passed Bill 11-06-F, sponsored by Lucas Humble, to collect textbooks the university bookstore would not buy back and send them to Africa. Senators also unanimously passed Resolution 08-06-F, sponsored by Seth Norman, backing a university study of a computer-lab printing quota after administrators told SGA's Student Affairs committee how many pages some students were printing.

events.title: Senate heard Douglas Keen Hall was next for renovation
events.body: In a University Committees report to the senate, a member reported that the Student Life Foundation had discussed campus housing renovations and that Douglas Keen Hall would be the next residence hall to be renovated, within about three years. The same report covered a Budget Council discussion of rolling several student organizations' budgets, including SGA's, into the university's base budget.

documents.title: SGA Senate minutes, 28 November 2006
documents.summary: Minutes of the twelfth meeting of that senate, called to order with 22 of 31 senators present. President Robert Watkins's resignation was read into the record, with senators told Jeanne Johnson would be sworn in as president at the Dec. 5 Winter Banquet. The senate also passed a bill and a resolution, heard committee reports, and voted on semester awards.
documents.extract: President Robert S. Watkins "formally resigned from office."

executive.name: Robert Watkins
executive.note: Resigned 28 Nov 2006, per SGA's own senate minutes; earlier Herald coverage this site had followed gave 30 Nov.

executive.name: Amanda Allen
executive.note: Received the Charles A. Keown Award at the May 2007 banquet, SGA's highest honor.

executive.name: Jeanne Johnson
executive.note: Presided in this capacity at the 28 Nov. 2006 meeting, before her formal swearing-in as president at the 5 Dec. 2006 Winter Banquet.

committees.name: Campus Improvements
committees.note: Theiss stepped down as chair in late Nov. 2006 for another leadership position.

committees.name: Legislative Research Committee
committees.note: Acting as vice-chair at the 28 Nov. 2006 meeting.

senate.note: Jeanne Johnson served as a fill-in leader after Watkins' resignation and was elected president in her own right for 2007-08 at the May 2007 banquet. Senate size, officers and committee chairs per the 28 Nov. 2006 meeting minutes; 22 of 31 senators were present that night.

leaders.name: Jeanne Johnson
leaders.note: Overlaps the Johnathon Boles 2008 plate. Sole name on the plaque for this year and no competing entry, so almost certainly the president. Not yet confirmed against Herald election coverage.
profile: In the spring, as her administration ran the election to choose her successor, Johnson defended the one-week campaign window written into election codes she said were inherited from past administrations, warning that longer campaigns could hurt candidates' schoolwork and that "too much PR hurts." She pointed to new turnout efforts her administration tried, including holding the debate during SGA week, arranging extra credit for students who attended it, and adding candidate profiles and questionnaires to the SGA website.

events.title: Fifty senators write down what a lobbying trip felt like
events.body: After a student rally at the Capitol in Frankfort, dozens of SGA members each filed an individual written reflection, archived one per person. The richest first-person source in the entire collection.

events.title: Fall senate election drew 25 candidates for 20 seats
events.body: SGA reported record interest in its fall senate election, with 25 students running for 20 available seats, the most applications President Jeanne Johnson said she had ever seen. Elections were set for Sept. 19 and 20 through TopNet, with an informational table in Downing University Center on Sept. 18. Public relations director Liz Goddard said more competition would produce harder workers.

events.title: SGA co-sponsored mock gubernatorial election
events.body: SGA and the Office of the Secretary of State co-sponsored a mock gubernatorial election at Centennial Mall as part of Secretary of State Trey Grayson's Civic Literacy Initiative of Kentucky. The 127 students who voted chose challenger Steve Beshear over incumbent Gov. Ernie Fletcher, 74 to 50. President Jeanne Johnson and Executive Vice President Johnathon Boles called the event a success.

events.title: Resolution demanded more state funding for Western
events.body: At its Oct. 9 meeting SGA passed a resolution asking the state government to appropriate more money to Western, which had received 54 percent of the funding the Council on Postsecondary Education recommended for fiscal year 2008. President Jeanne Johnson argued that tuition increases to cover the shortfall hurt students. The resolution stated Western needed the full recommended amount to meet its 2020 educational goals.

events.title: SGA organized Walk Out Western budget protest
events.body: SGA sponsored Walk Out Western, asking students to leave class at 12:20 p.m. on Oct. 25 for a rally at the Colonnade to protest state budget cuts, with empty seats meant as a message to Frankfort legislators. President Gary Ransdell said he could not condone students walking out of class and doubted a single-campus protest would affect state funding. Johnson said other state universities declined to join but were watching how it worked at Western.

events.title: Committee proposed $1,995 educational video subscription
events.body: SGA's Academic Affairs Committee, chaired by Drew Eclov, prepared legislation to buy a roughly $1,995 subscription to United Streaming, a Discovery Channel-owned site with about 45,000 educational video clips that Eclov called a version of YouTube for higher education. The committee planned to survey students and professors before bringing it to a vote. SGA also scheduled a vote on a resolution placing $1,000 in a field trip fund to support learning outside the classroom.

events.title: Athletics director asked SGA for help on football attendance
events.body: Athletics Director Wood Selig came to the SGA meeting to ask senators for ideas on getting more students to football games as Western moved to the Football Bowl Subdivision, which required an average attendance of 15,000 to keep bowl eligibility. Senators suggested advertising on Western's website and Facebook rather than email, and later game times. Executive Vice President Johnathon Boles, who sat on a faculty advisory committee for athletics, arranged the consultation.

events.title: SGA planned Listen Up Legislators lobbying campaign
events.body: SGA began laying groundwork for Listen Up Legislators, a spring lobbying campaign in which senators would meet legislators one-on-one in Frankfort to push for university funding, after the Council on Postsecondary Education recommended a $174 million increase for public universities. Chief of staff Skylar Jordan said the traditional February rally had not worked, pointing to Western receiving only 54 percent of the recommended increase. Other state student governments expressed interest in coordinating lobbying dates.

events.title: Spring session opened with ONE Campus bill
events.body: At its first spring meeting on Jan. 29, SGA introduced legislation by Senators Matt Vaughan and Doug Tate asking the senate to recognize Western as a ONE Campus, part of the national campaign against global AIDS and extreme poverty. SGA also released its spring schedule, including Listen Up Legislators on Feb. 14, the Frankfort rally for higher education on Feb. 20 and the annual banquet on April 29. In the semester's opening handout, Executive Vice President Johnathon Boles pointed members to the constitution's purpose of serving the student body equally.

events.title: Spring election closed amid low-turnout criticism
events.body: Voting for three executive seats and 28 senate seats ended after a one-week campaign that candidates criticized as part of SGA's low-involvement problem; turnout had been 1,424 the year before and 1,376 the year before that. Red Towel Party presidential candidate Tedde Harden promised to rework what he called outdated election codes, while opponent Johnathon Boles agreed campaign time should be extended. President Jeanne Johnson said her administration inherited the codes and had tried new turnout methods, including extra credit for attending the debate.

events.title: Ransdell announced 9 percent tuition increase
events.body: President Gary Ransdell announced at campus forums that he would recommend a 9 percent tuition increase for 2008-09, abandoning a plan to hold increases at 6 percent. The change followed a state budget crisis in which Gov. Steve Beshear ordered a 3 percent cut to postsecondary education in December 2007 and proposed an additional 12 percent, later reduced by the General Assembly to 3 percent. Ransdell said the swing from expected state revenue was about $11 million to $12 million.

leaders.name: Johnathon Boles
leaders.note: Confirmed against Herald election coverage. Boles led the "Red Towel Party" ticket - with Theodore Harden, Reagan Gilley, Skylar Johnson, Kayla Shelton and Kevin Smiley also on the March 2008 candidate slate - in the spring 2008 SGA election. After the vote, Skylar Jordan filed a complaint against the Red Towel Party; the SGA council took no action on it on 22 April 2008, letting the result stand. In office for the February 2008 Frankfort rally, after which roughly fifty senators each filed a written reflection - the richest first-person source in the collection. The Herald's 2013 retrospective records that Boles resigned in January 2009.

profile: Johnathon Boles ran for SGA president in spring 2008 on the "Red Towel Party" ticket, a slate that also carried Theodore Harden, Reagan Gilley, Skylar Johnson, Kayla Shelton and Kevin Smiley as candidates for other executive and senate offices. After Boles's ticket won, Skylar Jordan filed a complaint against the Red Towel Party; the SGA council took no action on it on 22 April 2008, and the result stood. Boles, a junior from Elizabethtown, served as SGA president and student regent for 2008-09. In November 2008, Gov. Steve Beshear appointed him and fellow SGA member Kevin Smiley to the student committee of the governor's College Access Work Group on college affordability, and Boles traveled to Frankfort for its first meeting, where he raised the burden of textbook costs. "I'm honored the governor chose me to represent WKU," he said.

In December 2008, Boles led SGA through its first mid-year budget cut, after a state shortfall required the university to trim about 4 percent. He and Administrative Vice President Reagan Gilley cut $4,100 from SGA's $110,000 budget while protecting scholarships and Provide-A-Ride, and Boles addressed the senate about the cuts, saying he would keep fighting for the affordability of higher education. He also worked to arrange charter buses to a Feb. 3 rally in Frankfort against cuts to higher education.

Boles resigned on Jan. 30, 2009, for health reasons, midway through his term. Executive Vice President Kayla Shelton took his place as president but not as student regent, and the student body went 26 days without a regent until Reagan Gilley won a special election on Feb. 25. Gilley said he planned to contact Boles the day after his win to get up to date on Board of Regents business.

leaders.name: Kayla Shelton
leaders.note: Plaque plate reads "2009" and had been filed under 2009-10, overlapping Kevin Smiley there; moved to 2008-09. Shelton was executive vice president on Johnathon Boles's Red Towel Party ticket and became president - but not student regent - when Boles resigned on 30 Jan 2009, finishing out his 2008-09 term. Kevin Smiley won the next regular election on 16 April 2009 for the 2009-10 term, so Shelton's presidency did not extend into 2009-10.

sources.label: College Heights Herald 83:42, 27 Mar 2008 - candidate coverage naming Shelton on the Red Towel ticket

profile: Kayla Shelton ran on Johnathon Boles's "Red Towel Party" ticket in the spring 2008 SGA election and served as executive vice president for 2008-09. When Boles resigned as president and student regent on 30 Jan. 2009 for health reasons, Shelton succeeded him as president but not as student regent, leaving the regent seat vacant.

As president, Shelton backed the SGA Judicial Council's 2-1 decision to hold a special student regent election rather than leave the seat vacant, over the dissent of Executive Vice President Skylar Jordan, saying "That's what they decided, so I support it" and that her main focus remained serving the student body. She also accepted Chief Justice Lisa Kappler's resignation in mid-February, which came with the regent election two weeks away. Administrative Vice President Reagan Gilley won that special election on 25 Feb. 2009, taking over the regent's seat while Shelton continued as president through the rest of the term.

Shelton presided over the senate through the spring, including a Feb. 24 meeting where senators debated and rejected, 13 votes to 9, a bill to cover an extra $82.27 for water bottles SGA had earlier agreed to fund as prizes for a Housing and Residence Life energy-saving contest. Shelton said she thought it was great that the senate debated something it felt passionate about rather than casting "just a general yes or no."
Shelton did not continue as president into 2009-10; Kevin Smiley won the regular spring election for that term on 16 April 2009.

events.title: Fall senate election drew above-average turnout
events.body: SGA seated nine new student senators after a two-day fall election in which 18 candidates competed. Seven seats had been open, four reserved for freshmen, and two more opened when two senators resigned the Monday before the vote. A total of 687 students voted, which President Johnathon Boles said was higher than the average for a fall election.

events.title: Boles and Smiley appointed to governor's college affordability group
events.body: Gov. Steve Beshear appointed SGA President Johnathon Boles and SGA member Kevin Smiley to the student committee of his College Access Work Group, which was charged with recommending ways to make Kentucky higher education more affordable. The two traveled to Frankfort for the committee's first meeting, where they raised the impact of textbook costs, which Boles put at an average of $800 a year.

events.title: Senate voted to launch a Textbook Subsidy Program
events.body: The SGA senate voted to contribute $500 to start a Textbook Subsidy Program, an effort developed with the University Bookstore, which pledged another $500, to build an endowment that would lower textbook costs for students. The senate also created a program board of nearly 20 members, including Boles, bookstore representatives and members from each college, to work out funding and distribution.

events.title: SGA made its first mid-year budget cut
events.body: Facing a state shortfall that required the university to cut about 4 percent of its budget, SGA cut $4,100 from its $110,000 budget, the first time it had cut its budget in the middle of an academic year. Boles and Administrative Vice President Reagan Gilley chose to cut a $2,600 surplus from the fall retreat and $1,500 from organizational aid, protecting scholarships and Provide-A-Ride. Boles said he was working to get charter buses to send students to a Feb. 3 rally in Frankfort against higher education budget cuts.

events.title: Judicial Council ordered a special student regent election over executive dissent
events.body: After Boles' resignation left the student regent seat empty, the SGA Judicial Council voted 2-1 on Feb. 10 to hold a special election on Feb. 24 and 25. Chief Justice Lisa Kappler cast the dissenting vote, calling the constitution's requirement a gray area, and Executive Vice President Skylar Jordan presented a letter arguing the election was unnecessary. President Kayla Shelton said she supported the council's decision.

events.title: Chief Justice Lisa Kappler resigned
events.body: SGA Chief Justice Lisa Kappler resigned Thursday night in a letter sent to President Kayla Shelton and student activities director Charley Pride, saying she wanted to spend more time on school and family. Shelton said she hoped the senate would vote on a new chief justice at the next meeting because the special election for student regent was two weeks away.

events.title: Reagan Gilley won the special student regent election
events.body: Administrative Vice President Reagan Gilley, a Pineville senior, defeated Speaker of the Senate Nate Eaton 477 votes to 224 in the special election for student regent, with 701 students voting. The seat had been vacant for 26 days after former President Johnathon Boles resigned on Jan. 30 for health reasons; Executive Vice President Kayla Shelton had taken his place as president but not as regent.

events.title: Kevin Smiley won the SGA presidential election
events.body: The Herald reported Kevin Smiley's win in the spring SGA presidential election under the headline "All Smiles, Kevin Smiley Wins Student Government Association Election," ending Kayla Shelton's term as the president who had finished out Johnathon Boles's 2008-09 year. Smiley took office as president and student regent for 2009-10.

events.title: SGA negotiated removal of proposed $30 per-credit-hour fee
events.body: SGA and university officials agreed to strike a proposed $30 fee for every credit hour over 15 from the Board of Regents agenda, replacing it with a proposal to raise the add/drop fee from $20 to $50. SGA canceled a planned protest after the compromise, and Student Regent Reagan Gilley called the outcome "really a win-win for everyone."

events.title: Ice storm hit campus, injuring a student and closing regional campuses
events.body: A winter storm coated campus in ice during the week of Jan. 27, part of the second-largest power outage recorded in Kentucky. A falling tree limb struck a sophomore near Grise Hall, who was treated and released, and WKU canceled classes at its Elizabethtown, Owensboro, Glasgow, Fort Knox and Radcliff campuses as well as evening classes on the main campus. AT&T cell outages kept officials from reaching students by text message.

events.title: Shots fired outside Pearce-Ford Tower put dorms on lockdown
events.body: Campus police responded to a report of shots fired at about 3 a.m. Saturday in the Pearce-Ford Tower parking lot, where a witness said a man got out of a vehicle, fired a gun and drove away. Police found shell casings but no damage, no one was hurt, and all dorms went into lockdown after the incident.

leaders.name: Kevin Smiley
leaders.note: Confirmed against Herald election coverage: Smiley won the SGA presidential election on 16 April 2009. The plaque's separate "2009" plate for Kayla Shelton is not a competing 2009-10 term - Shelton was finishing Johnathon Boles's 2008-09 term after his January 2009 resignation and has been moved to that year. By this period the SGA president automatically held the student regent seat.

profile: Kevin T. Smiley, a senior from Danville, served as SGA president and student regent for 2009-10. His executive branch included Executive Vice President Kendrick Bryan, Administrative Vice President Justin Thurman, and four appointed officials, among them his brother Eric Smiley as chief of staff.

Smiley opened his term with controversy in September 2009 when he nominated his brother, Danville sophomore Eric Smiley, for the paid chief of staff position, saying he chose him because he had no previous political agenda and was "somebody I truly trust." Former executive vice president Skylar Baker-Jordan called the move "completely unethical," though Thurman defended the president's right to pick a qualified adviser.

In October 2009 three senators resigned after Smiley nominated Greg Capillo to the Student Publications Committee, with Michel Stephens charging the pick was not based on merit. Smiley called the accusations of favoritism and corruption unfounded, described the resignations as a misunderstanding, and said he would begin contacting fall election candidates to fill the vacant seats. His term ran through the April 2010 election of his successor.

events.title: Smiley nominates his brother as chief of staff
events.body: SGA President Kevin Smiley announced Danville sophomore Eric Smiley, his brother, as his nominee for chief of staff, a paid voting position on the executive cabinet. Former executive vice president Skylar Baker-Jordan called the nomination "completely unethical," while Smiley said he chose his brother because he had no previous political agenda. The senate was set to vote on all nominations Sept. 8, with a two-thirds majority needed for approval.

events.title: Fall election opens; SGA gives $2,000 to Residence Hall Association
events.body: At the Sept. 15 senate meeting, Administrative Vice President Justin Thurman reported that SGA gave $2,000 from its budget to the Residence Hall Association. President Kevin Smiley announced that voting in the fall SGA election had started on TopNet, with polls open until Wednesday night and results announced about midnight. Smiley also urged senators to join the Campus Safety Walk, in which participants looked for dimly lit or overgrown areas on campus.

events.title: SGA sponsors forum on new tailgating policy
events.body: About 30 people attended an SGA-sponsored forum where students and administrators discussed Western's amended tailgating policy, which banned vehicles from campus lawns on game days. Howard Bailey, vice president for student affairs, told students the policy would stay the same, and Speaker of the Senate Wade Pierce suggested tent giveaways to ease the transition. President Kevin Smiley said he was pleased with the attendance and that SGA would keep questioning the policy.

events.title: Three senators resign over publications committee appointment
events.body: Senators Michel Stephens, Emmett Stephens and Daniel Shaw resigned at the Oct. 20 meeting. Michel Stephens cited President Kevin Smiley's nomination of Greg Capillo to the Student Publications Committee, which helps choose the Herald's editor-in-chief, saying the pick was not based on merit or experience. Smiley called the accusations of favoritism and corruption unfounded and said the seats would stay vacant until he appointed replacements for senate approval.

events.title: Judicial Council removes senator for unexcused absences
events.body: Chief Justice Stuart Kenderes reported that the Judicial Council removed Senator Theodore Harden, a graduate student from Otisville, N.Y., from SGA for excessive unexcused absences; Harden did not attend the council meeting to defend himself. The council also reviewed Senator Vashae Swope for absences but voted to let her remain. Attendance guidelines were posted in the SGA office window, and Rachel Wilcox was approved as a new senator at the same meeting.

events.title: WKU begins weighing a smoke-free campus
events.body: After the University of Kentucky and the University of Louisville went smoke-free, the Faculty Welfare Committee of Western's University Senate prepared a smoking survey for students, faculty and staff to take in February. SGA President Kevin Smiley said he would encourage the whole campus to take the survey, and President Gary Ransdell said he would look to SGA, the University Senate and Staff Council for direction on any policy.

events.title: Two more senators resign; Frankfort rally buses announced
events.body: At the Jan. 27 meeting, Aaron Pawley and Eileen Forsythe resigned as senators, Pawley because of a difficult course load and Forsythe because she was studying abroad in England. President Kevin Smiley announced free buses to carry 75 students to a Feb. 9 rally in Frankfort where advocates from Kentucky's public universities would lobby legislators on higher education funding. Western student Colton Jessie was slated to speak at the rally.

events.title: SGA organizes trip to Rally for Higher Education
events.body: SGA and the Provost's office offered free bus transportation for 75 students to the Rally for Higher Education on Feb. 9 at the Kentucky State Capitol, a year after winter weather derailed the previous attempt. Students who registered through the SGA website received an excused absence, and the rally included a chance to meet lawmakers and hear an address from Gov. Steve Beshear.

events.title: SGA passes election codes and two funding bills
events.body: The senate passed the spring 2010 election codes, a bill giving $500 to the Agriculture Students Striving for Effective Tomorrows conference for high school students, and a bill designating $1,200 for lodging for FIJIs Across America, in which eight Phi Gamma Delta members planned to cycle across the country for Alzheimer's research. Administrative Vice President Justin Thurman reported that all but three approved organizations had received their organizational aid checks.

events.title: Colton Jessie elected SGA president for 2010-11
events.body: Bowling Green junior Colton Jessie won the SGA presidency with 63 percent of the vote, taking 726 votes to 424 for Administrative Vice President Justin Thurman, on a platform of sustainability, handicap accessibility and changing the tailgating policy. Kendrick Bryan was re-elected executive vice president with 731 votes to Currie Martin's 415, and Wade Pierce ran unopposed for administrative vice president with 1,016 votes. Results were announced at midnight Wednesday.

leaders.name: Colton Jessie
leaders.note: Named as SGA president throughout the year's Herald coverage, including a dedicated year-end profile.
profile: Jessie opened the 2010-11 year having spent the summer preparing with his executive board, which attended the Kentucky Leadership Academy at Barren River State Park alongside SGAs from Kentucky's other public universities. His early priorities included building a closer relationship with international students, whom SGA hosted at a dinner during orientation, planning a study away program for students to study elsewhere in the country, and setting up a forum for South Campus concerns. "We are trying to reach out to South Campus," he said, and he and Executive Vice President Kendrick Bryan reallocated the budget to fund scholarship and study abroad programs.

By the end of his term, SGA had given out more scholarship money than ever, with the scholarship fund raised by $8,000 and organizational aid increased to $40,000, and the senate had passed first-of-their-kind bills reimbursing CLEP exam fees and buying test prep books for libraries. Jessie called the DUC renovation "one of the biggest things SGA has done in a while," and Ransdell credited him with taking the initiative to start the renovation talks. A senior, Jessie handed the office to Billy Stephens and left for Chicago after graduation to work for Teach for America.

events.title: SGA raised scholarship budget to $20,000
events.body: After running out of scholarship money the previous year, SGA increased its scholarship budget from $12,000 to $20,000 and lowered general senate funding from $20,000 to $12,000 to cover the change. Study abroad awards were capped at $500 for a semester trip and $250 for a winter or summer term so more students could receive money. SGA also finalized a new study away scholarship for travel inside the country and set aside $400 for it in the winter term.

events.title: Twelve senators elected in fall election with 847 voters
events.body: Twelve students won seats in the fall senate election, in which 847 total voters cast ballots on TopNet. Keyana Boka, Natalie Broderick and Eppiphanie Benton were elected freshman senators, running unopposed, while 25 students competed for the at-large seats. Winners included Diego Leal Ambriz, who would run for president that spring.

events.title: Ransdell brought $49 million DUC renovation plan to SGA
events.body: President Gary Ransdell and head architect Jeff Stivers told SGA at its Nov. 16 meeting that officials were moving ahead on a plan to completely renovate Downing University Center at a cost of up to $49 million. Students would pay about $140 extra per year in fees for up to 20 years, and Ransdell promised students would be involved in every decision. SGA had to pass resolutions on the design and fees before the Board of Regents could approve the project.

events.title: Senate tabled DUC resolution over lack of student input
events.body: Senators tabled the bill supporting the DUC renovation at the Dec. 7 meeting, saying they had not received enough student input just three weeks after learning of the project. Jessie backed the delay, saying he wanted to hear students' voices before moving forward, even though it pushed SGA's presentation to the Board of Regents from January 21 to April 22. Campus Improvements Chair Kaylee Egerer said many students did not yet know they would pay $140 a year for the project.

events.title: Herald reported Greeks held 40 percent of SGA seats
events.body: The Herald reported that 21 of SGA's 50 members belonged to Greek organizations, more than 40 percent, while less than 8 percent of the student body was in a fraternity or sorority. Sixteen of the 21 were fraternity men, and two fraternities, Sigma Chi and Lambda Chi Alpha, accounted for nine of them. Officers defended the imbalance, and the story noted SGA's operating budget for 2010-11 was $121,335, drawn from tuition.

events.title: SGA unanimously passed DUC renovation resolution
events.body: SGA unanimously passed the resolution supporting DUC renovations at its Feb. 22 meeting, the bill's second reading. Project costs were capped at $49,128,545, with a student fee of up to $70 per semester for 20 years and $1.5 million per year from WKU. The resolution, authored by Kaylee Egerer, asked for assurance of a 24-hour study space and called for construction to begin as soon as possible while interest rates were low.

events.title: SGA members joined Rally for Higher Education in Frankfort
events.body: SGA members traveled to Frankfort on March 1 for the annual Rally for Higher Education, where SGA secretary Katie Stillwell was the keynote speaker representing students statewide. Her speech urged legislators to protect money already set aside for higher education. Jessie, the previous year's keynote speaker, joined chief of staff Charlie Harris and other state SGA officers for a lunch with Gov. Steve Beshear.

events.title: Stephens won presidency with 56 percent of 1,066 votes
events.body: Billy Stephens, a junior from Hawesville, defeated senior Diego Leal Ambriz for SGA president, taking 56 percent of the 1,066 total votes in results announced just after midnight on April 7. Kendrick Bryan was re-elected executive vice president and Devon Hilderbrandt won administrative vice president, both unopposed. All 35 senate candidates were elected to the 36 open seats, each needing just one vote to win.

events.title: Senate tabled tobacco-free campus resolution
events.body: After nearly 45 minutes of debate, the senate tabled a resolution supporting a tobacco-free campus until the next semester. The resolution rested on a survey of more than 400 students in which 47.82 percent supported a ban, but senators argued the survey was biased because tombstones displaying the dangers of smoking had been laid outside DUC the day it was given. The campus improvements committee then said it would not support a ban until the two-year on-campus living requirement was removed.

events.title: SGA funds extended library hours for finals week
events.body: The senate approved $600 to keep the library open until 2 a.m. during finals week, covering extra staff time and lighting. President Colton Jessie said continuing the service was never in question, calling finals "an important time for students."

events.title: Administrative Vice President Wade Pierce to hand post to fraternity brother
events.body: Pierce, who chaired the organizational aid committee, said he would be succeeded as administrative vice president by Devon Hilderbrandt, his committee co-chair and his "little brother" in Lambda Chi Alpha. Hilderbrandt ran unopposed in that spring's election.

executive.name: Kendrick Bryan
executive.note: Re-elected unopposed to a second term as EVP for 2011-12.

executive.name: Wade Pierce
executive.note: Succeeded in 2011-12 by organizational aid co-chair and fraternity "little brother" Devon Hilderbrandt.

committees.name: Organizational Aid
committees.note: Co-chaired by Devon Hilderbrandt, who succeeded Pierce as administrative vice president in 2011-12.

senate.note: The Herald reported 50 total SGA members in February 2011, of whom 21 (more than 40 percent) belonged to Greek organizations against less than 8 percent Greek membership campus-wide.

leaders.name: Billy Stephens
leaders.note: Named as SGA president throughout the year's Herald coverage, from his April 2011 election through spring 2012 budget and personnel stories.
profile: Billy Stephens, a junior from Hawesville, was elected SGA president in the spring 2011 election, announced just after midnight on April 7. He defeated Diego Leal Ambriz, a senior from Monterrey, Mexico, with 56 percent of the 1,066 total votes. Outgoing president Colton Jessie called him "a fantastic candidate for the job," and Kendrick Bryan and Devon Hilderbrandt were elected unopposed as his executive and administrative vice presidents.

Stephens opened his term in August 2011 with a revamped public relations campaign built around asking students what SGA could do for them. "I want PR to be visible on campus," he said, complaining that new students often did not hear about SGA until the second semester. The campaign aimed to raise turnout in the fall senate elections, produce contested races and fill all 36 senate seats.

The fall brought open conflict: the senate voted down, 19-8, a resolution to rename Downing University Center that campus improvements chair Keyana Boka had written, the Herald editorial board told Stephens to focus on his own platform promises instead, two senators were dismissed for absences, and SGA was surprised by a $15,000 bill for the prior administration's unpaid Provide-A-Ride service. Chief of Staff Katie Stillwell resigned before the spring semester was out; Stephens replaced her with Eric Smiley, who had held the same post two years earlier under his brother's administration. The senate passed a spring budget of $50,026 in February 2012, down from $54,000 in fall spending.

events.title: SGA passes tobacco-free campus resolution with housing condition
events.body: The SGA senate voted unanimously for a resolution supporting a campus-wide tobacco ban, but only if WKU dropped its requirement that students live on campus for two years. President Gary Ransdell had said the Board of Regents would not consider a ban until SGA, the University Senate and Staff Council all passed resolutions. SGA was the only body to attach the housing stipulation.

events.title: Fall senate election fills 11 seats with 977 votes cast
events.body: SGA announced its fall senator election results just after midnight on Thursday, with 11 new senators elected including Christopher Costa, Corey Johnson and Mallory Treece. Twenty students ran for the seats and 977 students voted. President Billy Stephens said he was happy with the turnout for a fall election and that he got the contested race he wanted.

events.title: Senate defeats DUC name change resolution 19-8
events.body: A resolution to rename Downing University Center as Downing Student Union, written by campus improvements chair Keyana Boka, was voted down 19-8 with one abstention after a lengthy open debate. Executive Vice President Kendrick Bryan suggested putting the question on the spring ballot, but senators noted architects working on the DUC renovation would need an answer sooner.

events.title: Herald editorial tells SGA to drop renaming and keep its promises
events.body: The Herald editorial board wrote that SGA should focus on student issues rather than renaming a building honoring former president Dero Downing, who had recently died. It said Stephens had barely addressed his platform promises, including a dead day before finals and an improved Provide-a-Ride service, which had seen no visible progress since SGA cut ties with Franklin Taxi.

events.title: Two senators removed for absences; ten faced judicial review
events.body: Ten of SGA's 36 senators were called before the judicial board during the fall semester for excessive absences from senate and committee meetings. Two of them, Kevin Adams and Kevin Preston, were dismissed from the senate after failing to attend their judicial hearings, which the council interpreted as intent to resign. The rest received warnings, and Stephens said he would appoint replacements to the two empty seats.

events.title: SGA pays surprise $15,000 bill for previous year's Provide-A-Ride
events.body: SGA paid Parking Services a $15,000 retroactive payment for the prior year's Provide-A-Ride service after Parking Services found no record of the previous administration's payment. The money was split evenly between the organizational aid and student scholarship funds, $7,500 from each. Stephens said he was "shocked" by the bill, while 2010-11 president Colton Jessie insisted his administration had budgeted the money.

events.title: SGA approves $50,026 spring budget after $54,000 fall spending
events.body: The senate approved a spring 2012 budget of $50,026, divided among operations, public relations, executive programming and senate programming, with $10,500 set aside for organizational aid and $12,000 for scholarships. Chief of Staff Katie Stillwell told senators SGA had spent about $54,000 in the fall, $15,000 of it the retroactive Provide-A-Ride payment.

events.title: Chief of Staff Eric Smiley approved after Stillwell's resignation
events.body: The senate approved President Billy Stephens' choice of Eric Smiley as chief of staff after Katie Stillwell resigned the post. Smiley had served as chief of staff two years earlier under his brother Kevin Smiley's administration. The same meeting funded several campus organizations, including $500 each to the Chinese Students and Scholars Association, the Geology Club and the Chinese Music Club.

executive.note: Won re-election unopposed after Katie Stillwell dropped out of the EVP race.

executive.note: Ran unopposed, succeeding his fraternity "big brother" Wade Pierce.

executive.note: Resigned before spring 2012 was out; succeeded by Eric Smiley on 28 Mar 2012.

committees.note: Authored the failed resolution to rename Downing University Center. Spelling of first name unverified against "Keyanna," used for the same person's later presidential term.

leaders.name: Cory Dodds

WKU Office of Scholar Development, 15 Nov 2012
